title: CRAC-B-07 High Discharge Temperature — Clogged Filter
root_cause: Clogged air filter restricting airflow across evaporator coil. Filter was overdue for replacement (last changed 5 months prior, schedule calls for quarterly replacement in this zone).
symptoms: Discharge temp reached 36°C. Zone B humidity rose from 44% to 56% over 35 min. Adjacent zone ambient temp up 1.2°C.
resolution: Replaced air filter (FLT-2248). Cleaned evaporator coil surface with compressed air. Discharge temp returned to 26°C within 20 min. Zone humidity normalised within 1 hour.
lessons_learned: Filter replacement schedule should be monthly in high-dust zones (B, C), not quarterly. Added CRAC-B-07 to monthly maintenance rotation.
similarity_basis: Same unit (CRAC-B-07), same alarm type (high discharge temp), same symptom profile (humidity rise in zone)

title: PDU-A-01 Voltage Sag — Degraded Capacitor
root_cause: Degraded capacitor in power conditioning stage. Capacitor in bay C showed electrolyte leakage consistent with end-of-life failure. Same PDU model batch (APC AP8853, manufactured 2019) as PDU-A-03.
symptoms: Voltage dropped from 228V to 221V intermittently over 20 min. UPS battery temp elevated by 1.8°C. Load on PDU stable — ruled out overload.
resolution: Replaced capacitor module (CAP-M12). Voltage stabilised immediately. Full load testing confirmed nominal operation.
lessons_learned: Vendor bulletin VB-2024-03 subsequently issued covering this capacitor batch. All PDU-A series units should be inspected per bulletin.
similarity_basis: Same equipment type (PDU, APC AP8853), same alarm type (voltage_fluctuation), similar voltage sag pattern and rate

title: PDU-A-02 Voltage Alert — False Alarm (Sensor Drift)
root_cause: Voltage monitoring sensor on PDU-A-02 had drifted by -4V due to calibration failure after firmware update. Actual voltage was nominal throughout. Confirmed by handheld multimeter cross-check.
symptoms: Alarm showed voltage at 217V. Handheld multimeter read 226V at the same bus bar. Discrepancy of 9V indicated sensor fault, not actual voltage issue.
resolution: Recalibrated voltage sensor via PDU management interface. Firmware rolled back to version 3.1.2. No parts replacement required.
lessons_learned: Always cross-check with handheld multimeter before dispatching for power anomalies. Firmware updates should be tested in staging before rollout.
similarity_basis: Same equipment type (PDU, Zone A), same alarm type (voltage_fluctuation) — included as counter-hypothesis (sensor drift)

title: Chiller Loop 2 Pump Failure — Cascading Thermal Event (Zones C+D)
root_cause: Primary circulation pump (Grundfos CM25-3) on Chiller-01 loop 2 seized due to bearing failure. Chilled water supply temperature rose from 7°C to 18°C over 25 min. All CRAC units on loop 2 (Zones C and D) lost cooling capacity simultaneously.
symptoms: 3 CRAC units in Zones C+D reported elevated discharge temps within 8 min of each other. Zone D humidity spiked to 68%. Rack inlet temps in Zone C reached 38°C before intervention. Individual CRAC alarms were the visible signal — chiller plant was the root cause.
resolution: Switched to backup chiller pump (standby CM25-3). Chilled water supply temp recovered to 9°C within 15 min. CRAC units recovered automatically once supply temp normalised. Primary pump replacement scheduled for following day. Total downtime: none — no servers were taken offline. Resolution time from first alarm to stable temps: 4 hours.
lessons_learned: Individual CRAC/zone alarms in this pattern are symptoms, not root cause. Cascading alarms across Zones C+D simultaneously should trigger chiller plant check before CRAC unit dispatch. Standby pump switchover procedure added to SOP-CRIT-001.
similarity_basis: Same zones (C+D), same alarm types (high_temperature + compressor_fault + high_humidity), same pattern of multiple simultaneous alarms, same chiller loop 2

title: CRAC-B-07 Low Refrigerant Charge
root_cause: Slow refrigerant leak at service port SP-B07-R (loose Schrader valve). R410A charge at 78% of nominal. Subcooling measurement confirmed insufficient refrigerant.
symptoms: Discharge temp reached 34°C. Filter was clean (recently replaced). Refrigerant pressure below nominal range on both high and low side gauges.
resolution: Tightened Schrader valve. Recharged R410A to nominal pressure. Leak test passed. Discharge temp returned to 27°C.
lessons_learned: If filter replacement does not resolve high discharge temp, proceed directly to refrigerant pressure check. CRAC-B-07 has history of loose service port fittings.
similarity_basis: Same unit (CRAC-B-07), high discharge temp — included as second-hypothesis context

title: UPS-A-01 Battery Overtemp — Ambient Temperature Spike
root_cause: CRAC unit serving Zone A was offline for scheduled maintenance. Ambient temperature in Zone A rose to 28°C, causing UPS battery temp to reach 31°C. No UPS fault — environmental cause.
symptoms: Battery temp rose from 22°C to 31°C over 2 hours. Corresponded exactly with CRAC maintenance window.
resolution: CRAC maintenance completed. Ambient temp returned to nominal. UPS battery temp normalised within 45 min.
lessons_learned: UPS battery temp alarms during CRAC maintenance windows are expected. Consider suppressing during planned maintenance periods.

title: CRAC-D-01 Compressor Fault — Low Refrigerant
root_cause: Refrigerant leak at condenser coil connection. Compressor fault triggered as a protective measure when refrigerant pressure dropped below minimum operating threshold.
symptoms: Compressor fault code E04 (low pressure cutout). Discharge temp spiked to 45°C before unit shut down.
resolution: Located and repaired leak at condenser coil flare fitting. Recharged R410A. Unit restarted successfully. Full cooling restored in 3 hours.
lessons_learned: Compressor fault E04 on Liebert CW102 almost always indicates low pressure / refrigerant issue. Check refrigerant before investigating other causes.
similarity_basis: Same equipment type (CRAC, Zone D), compressor_fault alarm

title: CRAC-C-05 High Discharge Temp — Dirty Condenser Coil
root_cause: Condenser coil fouled with dust accumulation, reducing heat rejection efficiency. Discharge temp climbed to 37°C over a 6-hour period.
symptoms: Gradual discharge temp increase over 6 hours. Filter was clean. Refrigerant pressure nominal. Visual inspection revealed heavy dust on condenser coil.
resolution: Cleaned condenser coil with coil cleaner and compressed air. Discharge temp returned to 26°C. Added coil cleaning to quarterly maintenance checklist.
lessons_learned: Condenser coil cleaning not previously on maintenance schedule. Added to quarterly maintenance for all Zone C CRAC units.
similarity_basis: Same equipment type (CRAC, Zone C), high_temperature alarm — included for scenario completeness
